title: Broadcom Reports Earnings on Wednesday. The AI Boom, the Jobs Report, and a Possible Rate Hike All Converge in the Same Week.
excerpt: Broadcom's AI chip revenue grew 106 per cent last quarter. Analysts expect another blowout. But with PCE inflation at 3.8 per cent and the Fed meeting two weeks later, NRI tech investors face a week that could reset the narrative.
body:
If you hold US tech stocks — and if you are an NRI investor, the odds are high that you do — this week deserves your full attention. Three forces that have been building separately are about to collide in the span of five days.

On Wednesday, June 3, Broadcom reports fiscal second-quarter earnings. On Friday, June 5, the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the May employment report. And looming over both is the Federal Reserve's next rate-setting meeting on June 16-17, where the central bank will have to decide whether 3.8 per cent PCE inflation demands action.

Each of these events alone would move markets. Together, they amount to the most consequential week for US tech investors since the AI rally began accelerating in April.

## Broadcom: The AI Infrastructure Bellwether

Broadcom has become one of the clearest reads on whether the AI spending boom is real or whether it is beginning to crack. In the first quarter of fiscal 2026, the company reported AI semiconductor revenue of $8.4 billion, up 106 per cent year over year. Its custom AI accelerator business — the ASICs it designs for hyperscalers like Google and Meta — grew even faster.

Analysts expect the second quarter to be stronger. The consensus estimate is $2.32 earnings per share on revenue of approximately $22 billion. Broadcom has beaten earnings estimates in eight consecutive quarters.

But the bull case extends far beyond one quarter. CEO Hock Tan has guided for AI chip revenue exceeding $100 billion in fiscal 2027, implying a quarterly run rate of $25 billion — roughly triple the current pace. TrendForce estimates that ASIC shipments for AI servers will jump 45 per cent this year, outpacing GPU growth. Broadcom controls 60 per cent of that market.

The stock hit an all-time high of $448.90 on Friday, up 82 per cent in the past twelve months. Susquehanna raised its price target to $490, Aletheia Capital to $525, and UBS to $490. The consensus rating is Moderate Buy.

## The NRI Portfolio Problem

Indian-origin tech professionals in the US are disproportionately concentrated in semiconductor, cloud, and AI-adjacent companies. Many hold Broadcom, Nvidia, AMD, and related stocks through company equity plans, 401(k) allocations, or individual brokerage accounts. When these stocks move, NRI portfolios move with them.

The Dell earnings last week illustrated both the opportunity and the risk. Dell's AI server revenue jumped 757 per cent, and the stock gained 33 per cent in a single day. But the week before, signs of enterprise AI spending fatigue had pushed several software names lower. The market is rewarding companies with proven AI revenue and punishing those with AI promises but no receipts.

Broadcom's report on Wednesday will either confirm that infrastructure-layer demand remains robust or raise questions about whether the biggest customers are starting to moderate their spending. Either outcome will ripple through the entire AI supply chain.

## The Jobs Report and the Rate Hike Shadow

The May employment situation report on Friday could determine the Fed's next move. Economists expect 105,000 new nonfarm payrolls, down from 115,000 in April, with the unemployment rate holding at 4.3 per cent.

The context is what makes this number loaded. PCE inflation hit 3.8 per cent in April — nearly double the Fed's 2 per cent target — driven largely by higher energy prices from the Iran conflict. Money markets are now pricing a 25-basis-point rate hike in December and have priced out any rate cuts for the rest of the year.

A strong jobs report would increase the probability of a rate hike, which would pressure tech valuations. A weak report would raise recession fears, which would also pressure tech — but for different reasons. The narrow path for bulls is a number close to consensus: strong enough to avoid recession anxiety, soft enough to keep the Fed from acting sooner.

## What NRI Investors Should Watch

Three specific data points matter this week:

**Broadcom's AI revenue guidance for the full year.** The current run rate implies approximately $38 billion for fiscal 2026. If management revises this upward, the stock and the broader AI trade will rally. If it holds steady or moderates, expect profit-taking.

**The nonfarm payrolls number.** Anything above 150,000 strengthens the rate-hike case. Anything below 80,000 triggers slowdown fears. The sweet spot is 90,000 to 120,000.

**Fed commentary.** The Beige Book drops on Wednesday, the same day as Broadcom's report. Kansas City Fed President Schmid warned last week that the energy shock may not be temporary. Vice Chair Bowman said persistent inflation might require tighter policy. Any shift in tone matters.

For NRI investors with concentrated tech positions, this is a week to decide whether to hold, trim, or hedge. The AI fundamentals remain strong, but the macro environment is turning less accommodating. That tension will not resolve by Friday — but the data this week will tell you which direction it is leaning.
author: Diaspora Desk
